http://www.bgnes.com/european-union/fico.text: BGNES European Union Fico warns EU against treating China as an enemy, rejects shortcuts for Ukraine Fico warns EU against treating China as an enemy, rejects shortcuts for Ukraine 26.08.2026 - 07:58 Share BGNES The Slovak prime minister said his country was concerned about the EU's ability to compete globally. Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico has urged the European Union to pursue "friendly" competition with China rather than treating Beijing as an enemy and erecting new trade barriers, CGTN reported. Fico made the remarks after talks in Bratislava with European Council President Antonio Costa, who began his annual tour of EU capitals in Slovakia. The Slovak prime minister said his country was concerned about the EU's ability to compete globally. He argued that improving competitiveness should not mean imposing new tariffs or barriers, but rather striving to achieve better results. "I have a different view of relations between the EU and China. I do not think we should fight China by erecting barriers and treating it as an enemy," Fico said. "China is a country with which we should compete in a friendly spirit and strive to be better." The two leaders also discussed the EU's next long-term budget, competitiveness, energy prices and the bloc's future enlargement. On the EU budget, Fico said Slovakia supports maintaining a strong cohesion policy to reduce regional disparities across the bloc. He also called for additional funding for eastern EU member states, particularly those sharing borders with Ukraine. "We even say that additional funding should be found for the countries in the eastern part of the EU that, for example, share borders with Ukraine," he said. Fico also identified a strong agricultural policy as another key priority for Slovakia. On EU enlargement, the Slovak prime minister reiterated his country's support for candidate countries seeking membership, but stressed that all applicants must meet the required criteria. "This means no exceptions and no shortcuts. And this also applies to Ukraine," Fico said. He argued that Ukraine should not be allowed to overtake countries such as Montenegro, Albania or Serbia in the accession process, noting that those countries have been preparing for EU membership for much longer. | BGNES Follow us also on Watch and Comment news Comment in X More from European Union EU allows Ukraine to use €90bn loan funds to buy Patriot interceptors 08.09.2026 - https://www.politico.eu/article/scottish.text: LIVERPOOL — Scottish Labour’s new leader, Michael Marra, said he does not believe there is a “realistic prospect” of the U.K. rejoining the European Union because of “huge political instability” across the continent. Speaking at the POLITICO pub during Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, Marra argued that the changing political landscape in Germany and France meant the EU was not in a position to consider a British return “on any terms that we might think is reasonable.” Scotland’s governing Scottish National Party has repeatedly called for the U.K. to rejoin the bloc after 62% of Scots voted to remain in the EU in 2016. Advertisement Advertisement But Marra said that while he’d support a U.K. effort to rejoin should Europe find itself in a “different place” in the future, he admitted it may not be a “realistic prospect” for a generation or more. “Politics in Europe, I think, is really unstable at the moment. It’s facing many of the same challenges that we are in the U.K. in terms of the global economic instability, challenges in the Middle East, and migrant crises across parts of Europe have really destabilized politics.” Marra, who took over as leader after Labour suffered a humiliating defeat in May’s Scottish Parliament election, instead urged Prime Minister Andy Burnham to be “pragmatic” about forging closer links with the bloc. “What we do need is a closer relationship because we know the economic cost that’s resulted from Brexit. I want to see us doing that on a case-by-case basis,” he said. “Some of the things we’ve done around Erasmus and so on, I think that is a key thing.” His comments come amid growing debate among senior Labour ministers about the next steps in the U.K.’s relationship with Brussels at the party’s annual gathering in Liverpool. In a major intervention ahead of the conference, former Labour Prime Minister Tony Blair said there should be a plan to rejoin a “reformed EU” in the next decade. Andy Burnham has not yet ruled out including conditions for a fresh membership bid in his party’s next election manifesto, but is expected to expand on his approach when he speaks to the Labour faithful later today. https://www.scottishlegal.com/articles/c.text: Article Tags: echr belarus Council of Europe renews call for Belarus to abolish death penalty 13 Oct 2026 Reading time: 2 minutes Article Tags: echr belarus The Council of Europe has called on Belarus to halt executions as part of renewed efforts to abolish capital punishment across Europe. The call came as the organisation held its first event at its Information Point for Belarusians in Vilnius, Lithuania, yesterday, marking the World Day Against the Death Penalty, observed on 10 October. Belarus is the only country in Europe that still carries out executions. The Council of Europe has repeatedly opposed capital punishment in all circumstances. The Vilnius event brought together Council of Europe experts, diplomats and representatives of Belarusian civil society to discuss abolition. It forms part of the organisation’s work with Belarusian democratic forces and civil society, following the establishment of the Information Point in May 2026. A new website exploring the history of the death penalty in Minsk was launched at the event. It offers a virtual tour of locations associated with capital punishment in the Belarusian capital during the 20th and 21st centuries. Yuliya Ralko of the Belarusian National Youth Council (RADA) said: “The idea of this website came from the young participants of a workshop organised by the Council of Europe and RADA in May 2024 in Vilnius, as part of the Contact Group’s activities. We are very pleased to see this idea become a reality.” The Council of Europe’s Committee of Ministers adopted a decision on the death penalty on 7 October, condemning Belarus’s use of capital offences added to its criminal code in 2022 and 2023 to impose death sentences. It called on the Belarusian authorities to suspend all executions pending abolition and to apply alternative punishments already available under domestic law. The committee also welcomed a memorandum on abolishing the death penalty adopted by Belarusian democratic forces in June 2025. In a joint statement ahead of the World Day Against the Death Penalty, Council of Europe Secretary General Alain Berset and EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas reiterated their opposition to capital punishment in all cases and circumstances. Lesser/AFP Advertisement A Group of 20 foreign ministers' meeting in the US city of Atlanta got off to a rocky start on Friday after top diplomats from European nations refused to take a "family photo" along with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who is hosting the gathering, decided to scrap the photo before the meeting got underway because Washington didn't want it to become a spectacle or distraction. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul told reporters before the first session on Friday that there wouldn't "be a family photo with European partners and Mr. Lavrov together because ... there is no normalcy with Russia." The two-day gathering of the G20 grouping, which includes the EU, Russia, Germany, India, China, Brazil and other major countries, is meant to be a precursor to a G20 leaders summit later this December. That G20 leaders meeting in December is set to be hosted by US President Donald Trump at his golf club in Miami. G20 gathering is set to discuss issues like freedom of navigation in crucial trade routes and energy supplies Image: Michael Kappeler/dpa/picture alliance German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul pledged to "call on Russia to finally accept Ukraine's offer of a ceasefire, starting in the Black Sea" Image: Megan Varner/REUTERS Rubio stresses unity despite fractures Rubio still opened the talks by stressing unity on major issues, telling his counterparts that they were in a "critical moment." "We are facing a series of interconnected economic and geopolitical crises," he said. He pointed to disruptions to global energy and trade and said many were posing "severe threats to essential foundations of the global economic order." But several countries, including the United States and Russia, are involved in separate wars. Wars in Iran and Ukraine have resulted in a spike in food prices for people around the world . While the message is about unity and finding solutions to problems like freedom of navigation in the Black Sea and the Strait of Hormuz during the G20 meeting, the reality is that finding common ground will likely be much tougher. Given a renewed momentum to revive talks to end the war in Ukraine , there was also interest in getting Lavrov to talk about Russia's stance on future talks with Kyiv. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio appealed for unity between members of the G20, despite the US not inviting all of them to the ministers' meeting Image: Erik S. Lesser/AFP Russia willing to meet Zelenskyy in Moscow, Lavrov tells DW The US has invited Russian President Vladimir Putin to the G20 meeting in Miami, but it's unclear whether Russia has accepted the invitation. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has previously said that he would be open to traveling to Miami to hold talks with Putin if he were also there. The Kremlin has so far declined direct meetings with Zelenskyy, with Russia's Sergey Lavrov telling DW on the sidelines of the meeting that Putin is willing to meet with the Ukrainian leader if he travels to Moscow. "President Putin said if he [Zelenskyy] is willing to meet, let him come to Moscow," Lavrov said. "We will guarantee his safety." Lavrov declined to say whether Putin will attend the G20 summit this December. Putin has not attended a G20 leaders meeting since 2019 and only attended a session virtually in 2023. Russia has also continued with its attacks on Ukrainian cities in recent weeks , stepping up drone strikes on water and energy infrastructure. A Russian drone strike on a railway station in Dnipro on October 29 killed at least 14 people Image: Telegram channel on president ou Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyj EU top diplomat calls out Lavrov's 'lies' The European Union's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said ministers at the G20 meeting were able to call out Lavrov for his "lies" at the table. "We were talking about the big geopolitical crises, including Ukraine, and we were able to address Sergey Lavrov head-on with this," Kallas said on the sidelines of the meeting. "Of course, he put forward a lot of lies, a lot of false narratives that we were also able to then rebuke," she said. British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband also called out Lavrov, saying, "If we are serious about our values and our interests, we must also work harder to secure just and lasting peace in Ukraine." Lavrov says no easing of ties with US, 'no illusions' about diesel deal Lavrov, who is under international sanctions for Russia's war in Ukraine , was invited to the US at a time when the two countries have appeared to have fostered warmer ties. Trump announced a diesel deal with Russia earlier this month and also waived new sanctions on Russia's energy. The US announced the move just weeks away from the midterm elections on November 3. Lavrov said on Friday that despite those efforts, "in practice, no real progress in relations with the US has so far been seen." Ukraine, which is not a G20 member but was invited to attend previous such meetings, was not invited this year because US officials said they made a conscious choice to include only formal members of the group. But US officials didn't extend that invite to South Africa, a G20 founding member and the only African country in the group. "We have consistently maintained that our nonparticipation is not voluntary," said Phindile Kunene, spokesperson for South African Foreign Minister Ronald Lamola. With this many issues on the table, it appeared less likely that there would be a joint consensus at the end of the talks. Instead of a final declaration, the AFP news agency reported, the meeting is expected to end on Saturday with a chair summary drafted by the US.
